paragraphs: Here's what I love about this psalm, friend. Asaph doesn't pretty up his night. He cries aloud, he can't sleep, and he says his soul "refused to be comforted" (Psalm 77:2). Then he asks the hard questions out loud: "Has God forgotten to be gracious?" (Psalm 77:9). I think that's a man who trusts God enough to bring Him the whole mess.

Then the turn. Asaph says, "I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old" (Psalm 77:11). He doesn't get a quick answer to his questions. He gets a decision: look back at what God has already done, and stay there a while. He says he'll "reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds" (Psalm 77:12), and that is NOT a quick glance.

So when your night feels long, and the ceiling gets a lot of your attention, do what Asaph did. Take your hurting heart and your hard questions to God, then open the Word and remember what He has done. Asaph says God's footprints were not found in the sea (Psalm 77:19), but he still says God "led Your people like a flock" (Psalm 77:20). You can't always see Him walking, baker, but He is still leading. I'd say that's worth remembering, and I've got a whole bakery of ovens that agree.
